dialogues.title: Asking About the Bus
dialogues.sit: You are at a bus stop and want to go downtown.
lines: Excuse me, which bus goes to downtown?
The number 10 bus. It comes every 15 minutes.
Three dollars. You can tap your card or pay cash.
Yes, the bus does not give change.
Where do I tap my card?
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about the TRAIN instead.

dialogues.title: Riding the Bus
dialogues.sit: On the bus, not sure where to get off.
lines: Does this bus go to Main Street?
Yes. About ten stops from here.
Can you tell me when we get there?
No, this bus goes directly there.
dialogues.tp: Try again: you DO need to transfer.

dialogues.title: Getting Directions
dialogues.sit: You are lost and ask a passerby.
lines: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?
Go straight for two blocks, then turn left.
Yes, the one with traffic lights.
About a five-minute walk. Station is on your right.
Thank you! I am new here.
dialogues.tp: Try again: station is to the RIGHT, three blocks.

dialogues.title: Buying a Transit Pass
dialogues.sit: You go to buy a monthly transit pass.
lines: I would like to buy a monthly pass.
Zone one. How much is it?
Can I pay with credit card?
At the yellow readers on the bus and at station gates.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about a day pass instead.

dialogues.title: Talking About Commuting
dialogues.sit: Your coworker asks about your commute.
lines: How do you commute to work?
I drive. The highway takes 30 minutes.
I take the bus. About 45 minutes.
Not bad! Is it a direct route?
Maybe try a bicycle in summer!
Good idea! I might try that.
dialogues.tp: Try again: you commute by train, one hour.
dialogues.tn: 練習 commute, ride, drive, transfer。

culture.title: How Canadians Get Around
culture.photo: 📷 A busy transit station with buses and tap cards.
culture.notes: Most Canadian cities have buses and trains. Compass Card (Vancouver) and Presto (Toronto) are tap cards. In smaller cities, people mostly drive.
qs: How do people commute in your city?
Would you drive or take transit?
What surprises you about Canadian transit?

culture.title: Winter Transportation
culture.photo: 📷 A snowy street with buses running and icy sidewalks.
culture.notes: Canadian winters make commuting hard. Roads get icy and buses can be delayed. Many people use winter tires. Walking on ice is dangerous — wear boots with grip!
qs: Does it snow where you live?
What would you do if the bus was late in a snowstorm?
